name: CEAVOX
summary: Voting, elections and tickets in one place.
desc: An event platform bringing award voting, elections and ticketing into one digital experience.
label: Voting / Elections / Ticketing
challenge: Events bring different people into the same experience: organisers setting things up, participants registering and audiences voting or reserving a place. Each needs a clear route through the product.
contribution: I worked across the frontend and backend, connecting public participation journeys with the application logic and organiser tools behind them.
decisions: Award voting, elections and ticketing have distinct flows. The product brings them together while allowing each event type to work in its own way.
Public event pages and organiser workflows belong to the same product, so the work extends beyond the landing page into the interactions that follow.
journeys: Vote, register or get a ticket
outcome: A live product spanning three event formats. The public event discovery interface is shown here; visit the website to explore current events.

screens.title: The public introduction
screens.caption: A bold landing page introduces voting, elections and ticketing, with clear routes to create or discover an event.

screens.title: Finding an event
screens.caption: The discovery screen brings search, trending events and browsing filters into one place.

name: HearIntel
desc: An audiology platform connecting clinical patient management with a national hearing-health registry.
label: Clinical software / Registry
challenge: Clinical teams need tools for individual patient care, while a registry serves a different purpose: understanding patterns in hearing health. The platform needs to support both without confusing their users or information access.
contribution: I worked across the clinical and registry interfaces and their supporting backend, including data workflows, authentication, permissions and deployment.
decisions: The patient management module supports clinical workflows. The registry is designed to expose authorised aggregate or de-identified information, rather than patient care records.
Roles and facility membership guide which parts of the platform a user can access. Clinical information and registry views follow distinct permission boundaries.
outcome: A live audiology platform with a public introduction to its clinical and registry modules. This case study uses only the public landing page.

screens.title: The first impression
screens.caption: The public website introduces the platform and helps visitors find the right workspace.

screens.title: Two connected workspaces
screens.caption: The public platform overview explains clinical patient management and the separate registry purpose.

screens.title: The wider picture
screens.caption: The public registry introduction describes authorised aggregate and de-identified reporting. No patient records are shown.

name: QPrep
summary: A home for academic past questions.
desc: An academic past-question repository, with a signed-in experience for accessing study materials.
label: Education / Academic resources
challenge: Past-question materials need a useful place to live, with an interface that helps students orient themselves around their academic resources.
contribution: I handled full-stack development, working on both the visible interface and the application behind the education project.
decisions: QPrep centres on academic past questions, with course information providing context for its study resources.
The sign-in interface provides a focused entry point to the repository, with a consistent visual identity across its account controls.
outcome: A live academic past-question repository. The sign-in page provides the entry point to its education experience.

screens.caption: A focused sign-in screen provides the entry point to QPrep.

screens.title: Creating an academic profile
screens.caption: The public registration interface gathers academic context, including institution and level. The form is shown empty; no account was created.

name: Safe Nest
desc: A housing and renting website introducing a brand built around renting independence.
label: Housing / Web experience
challenge: The first interaction with a housing brand needs to introduce its purpose clearly and offer an obvious next step, including on a phone.
contribution: I developed the public-facing website experience, with attention to the interface, responsive layouts and how visitors move through the site.
decisions: The opening screen combines a strong housing message, city imagery and a prominent call to action.
Responsive presentation makes the brand introduction and navigation usable across different screen sizes.
outcome: A live housing and renting website, with a clear brand introduction and a direct next step for visitors.

screens.title: A clear route into renting
screens.caption: The public homepage combines city imagery, a brand introduction and a search interface. My contribution was frontend development.

screens.title: Introducing shared living
screens.caption: A dedicated section uses imagery and a direct next step to explain the co-living offering.
